title: Holding More Than One Enrollment in the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans
content:
A retiree may hold only one group retiree enrollment under any one sponsor at a time, though a person who worked for two employers may hold one under each. At most 2 group retiree enrollments stand for one retiree at one time in the Employer and Union Group Retiree Plans book.

## What must be so before a new enrollment record is opened

No other group retiree enrollment for the same member under the same group number is in a status of group file received, eligibility confirmed, active or premium arrears on the day the new record is opened.

The condition is settled on the plan's own enrollment records, and before the record is opened. What is read is the retiree named, the group contract they are named under, the standing of each enrollment and the contract year; what the retiree says they hold settles nothing. The records are read against the retiree the new record would name.

## When two enrollments are the same holding

Two enrollments are the same holding where they name the same retiree under the same group contract. A different contract year or a different first day of coverage makes them different holdings, and enrollments in different contract years that do not overlap are never duplicates.

Where a sponsor's file names a retiree who already holds an enrollment under that group, the file line is treated as a change to the enrollment they hold rather than as a new one.

## A retiree under two sponsors

A retiree holding enrollments under two sponsors is billed and serviced on each separately, and the plan tells them which group each benefit comes from whenever they ask.

## Points of judgement

The condition names four standings and no others. An enrollment standing at group terminated, or at disenrolled, is therefore not one of the standings that would make a second record under the same group contract a duplicate.

The condition asks about the same group number. Two enrollments held under different sponsors are held under different group contracts, so the condition never falls to be tested between them.
